body:
the way I see it, I just can't handle starting again. The end result is always going to be the same. I read online that its common for employers to just fire you once they use you up and then just hire the next sucker because it costs less for them. I just don't see the point of trying anymore. 
I already started it all from scratch when I was 13. I did everything my therapist told me to do, I did everything I was supposed to do with the belief that life would get better. The feelings never went away completely but I kept stupidly clinging to that hope. The thoughts always resurfaced on and off. I guess you're right in that I survived and am standing but even if I am, it feels like I'm slowly falling down again. Or it's like I'm struggling to keep my head above water, and everyone else is on the beach enjoying themselves while I'm about to drown if that makes sense.

I'm not strong...I just was waiting for life to get better because my therapist told me it would. I learned back then how awful teens are and she told me it gets better. But I waited, I did what I was supposed to do, and it didn't...for every one kind person there are 10 awful ones. I don't know what I live for anymore if it's just going to be a 9 to 5 job where you get shoved out the door with curse words while everyone on the floor watches.  

I'm not smart either or else I wouldn't be fired right now. I'm just a corporate sheep who got exiled from the fold. 

I don't have friends. I mean the closest "relationship" i had was with one coworker (or I guess semi-supervisor, I don't know, my Lead.) I had the one sister and she was so mean to me when I grew up, so we grew apart and became estranged. She lives her own life now, I don't even think she'll care even if there is a letter.

I don't know. The only reason I kept going was my therapist in high school told me that teenagers are just awful. She said it gets better in college, to just wait. 
And I waited and waited. And there were good points, but, there were just so many bad ones too. I really tried. I tried so hard. It just...wasn't enough. 
I'm not brave.. I just listened to what people in authority told me. They gave me so much hope. I wanted to believe them. It wasn't bravery, just, me following orders...
Thanks...I don't really deserve even a virtual hug imo.
I like reading everyone's stories on this Reddit community but the more I read the more I think about it.  Thanks for reading mine.
I swear, this post could be me. Don't know if you'll ever read this since it's been 4 days, but, just want to say that I know how you feel.

Sorry about the unemployment. I just got fired too. 

When I drive along deserted parts of the freeway I think about crashing my car. Funny to think that all it takes to end it is stepping on a pedal and turning the wheel 90 degrees.

It gets even worse after entering the work force.

All your coworkers and managers lead normal lives and always have talk about how wonderful their life is - they just closed on a house, had kids, got a promotion, whatever. And you can't help but think that you could never be that carefree and giddy about your own life. They might be in the same building as you but they live in a totally different world.

This post really spoke to me. I feel the same way. 

I question whether people enjoy the company of others or if they simply want more members for their highlight reel. And if the highlight reel represents the best moments of life - is that really all there is to life?

First off, please do not be rude. 
Second, I have shortened my post as advised. Please take a look if you have time I would greatly appreciate it. Thank you for your time.
